substantiveFit: The goal asks a bounded judgement from supplied quality documents. Its two essential expectations distinguish actual analytical findings, documented process/traceability evidence and the general statutory protective purpose. This operationalises part of the exact quality-control bullet without claiming to train all manufacture, clinical evaluation or authorisation work.

DossierX separates reference-compatible chromatographic evidence from missing method coverage/detection limits and absent batch/cleaning records. A compatible peak cannot establish total purity, GMP compliance or a real authorisation. Fresh analytical-selectivity changes remain open despite better records.

DossierY treats calibration within a valid method range and a current interfering blank separately from traceability and an unverified label. A corrected blank does not repair uncertain record attribution. This is genuine new evidence reasoning rather than recall of an approval label.

The supplied method card makes a concept judgement feasible without requiring unsupported real drug manufacture or an independent legal/clinical decision. Any wider practical/source-process duties remain separate.
